review_notes: I read the whole 41-line file. It has three theorems. The first two prove the two directions of one equivalence: commuting with xm is equivalent to commuting with rootOp. They use different arguments. The first applies endo, expands the product, cancels, and divides by the nonzero scalar. The second goes the other way and uses injectivity of endo. The third theorem reduces to xm at 1 by base change and then applies the first two lemmas. Together these are already the shared machinery, so nothing is repeated across proofs. The only short repeated pattern is applying endo and simplifying with endo_mul and endo_xm. That is a routine simp call and too small to count under the rubric. I did not look at other files for duplicated blocks, because the rubric asks about repetition within this file's proofs.
